newsitem.title: USA: D.C. airport partially evacuated, gas fumes detected.
newsitem.headline: D.C. airport partially evacuated, gas fumes detected.

text.p: Washington's National Airport was partially evacuated and flights were diverted to a nearby airport on Sunday after gas fumes were detected in the lobby of the main terminal, an airport spokeswoman said.

The spokeswoman said the local gas company, Washington Gas, had arrived on the scene, turned off the gas and was investigating, but it was unclear what caused the fumes in the lobby, which houses the ticket counters of United Airlines, Air Canada and Trans World Airways (TWA).
Six flights had been diverted to Washington Dulles International Airport, she said.
Passengers and airport employees were evacuated only from the lobby area, the spokeswoman said.

She said the incident appeared unrelated to a similar one several months ago in which a transit bus hit a gas pipeline in a tunnel on the airport grounds, forcing the evacuation of another smaller terminal and delaying flights for hours.
The fumes were first detected between 5:30 p.m. and 6 p.m., she said.
